- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 2–5% from forecast for 3–7 days post-spike.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model often underestimates; add 1–3% to forecast for next 5–10 days to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: if price is above 30-day moving average, forecast tends to overcorrect downward; if below, overcorrects upward — adjust by aligning forecast to 30-day MA ± 1–2%.
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses late-period momentum; if sentiment turns positive mid-horizon, adjust forecast upward by 1–2% for final 5–7 days.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model is prone to “noise” overfitting; use 3–5 day rolling average of sentiment to smooth forecast adjustments.
